You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc. realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (2018-2020)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed as the separated
> entity's (Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc.) realized 2018-2020 record, traced through
> its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2019 (filed 2020-03-30).
> This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Realized financial trajectory (primary-sourced scalars)
- The company reported a net loss attributable to stockholders of $121,974 thousand (~$122.0 million) for the year ended December 31, 2019, following a net loss attributable to stockholders of $725,292 thousand (~$725.3 million) for the year ended December 31, 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019) Consolidated Statements of Operations]
- Total net loss (before the attribution split) was $129,039 thousand for 2019 and $724,857 thousand for 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019) Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive (Loss) Income]
- A goodwill impairment of $40,046 thousand was recognized in 2018; no additional goodwill impairment was recorded thereafter through the reporting date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

## Documented disruption at the product/operations interface
- The company's Vølund & Other Renewable segment was the locus of severe operating losses: adjusted gross profit (loss) in that segment increased $247.2 million year over year to $9.0 million, implying a prior-period loss of roughly $238 million on its European renewable / waste-to-energy engineering-and-supply contracts. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- In response, the company changed its approach to bidding on and executing renewable energy contracts — refocusing on engineering and supplying its core waste-to-energy technology and electing to limit bidding on additional renewable energy contracts that involved its European resources while it worked through then-existing contracts. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

## Documented disruption at the operations/organization interface
- Substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern was disclosed, tied to a refinancing that had to be completed on or prior to May 11, 2020; management stated it was taking all prudent actions to address the substantial doubt. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- The recapitalization was backstopped by an outside financial party: pursuant to Amendment No. 20 to its Amended Credit Agreement the company entered into a backstop letter agreement with B. Riley Financial, Inc. (and affiliates) to support the refinancing/refinancing raise; the company's continuation was contingent on that backstop and on raising new capital. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- The capital structure was reset during the window: the company completed a Rights Offering on July 23, 2019 and a one-for-ten reverse stock split on July 24, 2019. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

## Portfolio actions within the window
- The company divested operations during 2019, including the sale of Loibl (a materials-handling / non-core business) and the sale of the MEGTEC and Universal businesses. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Over its 2018-2020 record the separated company posted consecutive large net losses (~$725.3 million attributable in 2018; ~$122.0 million attributable in 2019), recognized a 2018 goodwill impairment (~$40.0 million), and reached substantial-doubt-going-concern status requiring a May 2020 refinancing backstopped by an outside financial party (B. Riley Financial), a Rights Offering, and a one-for-ten reverse split; the losses centered on European renewable / waste-to-energy contracts that the company could not execute profitably and subsequently curtailed, alongside divestitures of non-core businesses. [SRC: SEC accession 0001630805-20-000026, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

[SLICE END]
